From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed trial acceptance criteria

Hi Liam + Priya,

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciated the clear context on the data flows and the two headline use cases (customer support triage + automated tagging). Per our call, attached is a focused trial acceptance checklist and a first-draft success-criteria workbook (orchid_trial_success_criteria.xlsx). High-level recap and asks: 

- Trial scope (2 weeks): Evaluate Redwood streaming API for low-latency classification and our SDK for server-side batching.
- Success criteria (proposed): 
  * Latency: p95 inference latency < 250ms for 256-token requests
  * Throughput: sustain 50 qps with 50% CPU headroom on their test cluster
  * Quality: macro-F1 >= 0.82 on your labeled validation set
  * Integration: end-to-end demo using SDK streaming + function/tool-calling to your tagging service
- Ownership: Redwood will own runtime config + SDK deliverable; Orchid to provide a ~5k labeled test set and a sandbox API for tagging.
- Tech asks: access to a sandbox API key, CORS/IP allowlist, and sample messages for prefix/KV cache tuning.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ben to own the SDK/streaming implementation and provide an integration diagram by 2027-04-22.
2) Orchid to provide test data and sandbox endpoint by 2027-04-23.
3) Kickoff engineering sync 2027-04-24 (30 min) — calendar invite pending.

If that all looks good I can send a compact mutual action plan and get the trial environment spun up.

Best,
Mina

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + proposed trial acceptance criteria — runtime & integration plan

Ben / team,

Draft runtime/config + recommended API surface below (high level):

1) SDK/Client recommendation
- Provide server-side SDK snippets (Node, Python) using Redwood streaming client. Main call: RedwoodSDK.streamGenerate({model: 'rw-infer-1', route: '/v1/stream/generate', streaming: true, toolCalls: true})
- Example: stream + function/tool calling for tagging service (we will include sample function schema for the tagging endpoint).

2) API routes (trial)
- POST /v1/stream/generate — streaming token responses (recommended for low-latency path)
- POST /v1/generate — batch-style non-streaming for bulk re-runs/quality evaluation
- POST /v1/embeddings — embeddings for similarity checks during evaluation

3) Runtime config suggestions
- Batching: bump continuous batching target to 40ms (for Orchid’s qps profile)
- KV cache TTL: 10m for session-level warm-starts
- Quantization: int8 profile if memory constrained; measure perf delta during initial ramp
- Fallback policy: pinned smaller model in Dedicated pool if p95 > 300ms for sustained 5 minutes

4) Metrics we'll surface for the acceptance gates
- p95 latency, throughput (qps), token cost per inference, macro-F1 on validation set, end-to-end tagging success rate

5) Integration deliverables & owners
- SDK examples (Ben) — Node + Python, plus a small Docker sample that runs a streaming demo (deliver 2027-04-22)
- Runtime config + fallback plan (Jordan) — deliver 2027-04-22
- Redwood to create an ephemeral trial API key and a CORS/IP allowlist template (Mina) — deliver 2027-04-23

6) Attachment: orchid_sdk_integration_diagram.png (calls out SDK -> streaming route -> function/tool call -> Orchid tagging API).

I’ll attach a short curl example in the repo and open a PR against the orchid branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/orchid

Jordan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
